title: Cells
seo_title: Year 7 Science: Cells Worksheets (Plant and Animal Cells, Microscopes)
standard_text: Cells as the fundamental unit of living organisms, including how to observe, interpret and record cell structure using a light microscope; the functions of the cell wall, cell membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus, vacuole, mitochondria and chloroplasts; the similarities and differences between plant and animal cells.
meta_desc: Free Year 7 science worksheets on cells: the parts of plant and animal cells and their jobs, labelled cell diagrams, and using a light microscope with magnification. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: All living things are made of cells.
key_sub: Plant cells also have a cell wall, chloroplasts and a large vacuole.
body_html:
How to think about it

All living things are made of cells.

  • Animal and plant cells have a nucleus, cell membrane, cytoplasm and mitochondria.
  • Plant cells also have a cell wall, chloroplasts and a large vacuole.
  • A light microscope magnifies cells: total magnification = eyepiece × objective.
Example

×10 eyepiece, ×40 objective. Total?

10 × 40

Answer: ×400

Example

Which part controls the cell?

Contains DNA

Answer: the nucleus

Common mistakes

  • Thinking animal cells have a cell wall.
  • Thinking mitochondria are only in animal cells.
  • Adding magnifications instead of multiplying them.

faq.q: What are the parts of an animal cell?
faq.a: A nucleus, cell membrane, cytoplasm and mitochondria.

faq.q: How is a plant cell different from an animal cell?
faq.a: A plant cell also has a cell wall made of cellulose, chloroplasts for photosynthesis and a large permanent vacuole.

faq.q: How do you work out magnification?
faq.a: Multiply the eyepiece magnification by the objective magnification. A ×10 eyepiece and ×40 objective give ×400.
